pages.run: Where your diagnosis stands, from your data to the answer, step by step.
pages.main: The answer in one place: which machine is your <bottleneck>bottleneck</bottleneck>, what it costs and how sure we are (<confidence>confidence</confidence>).
pages.loss: The hours and euros your <bottleneck>bottleneck</bottleneck> loses each week and month, and why.
pages.machines: How busy each machine really is: running, <setup>setup</setup>, down, <starved>starved</starved> or <blocked>blocked</blocked>.
pages.actions: What to do about your <bottleneck>bottleneck</bottleneck>, with the euros it could gain and what it costs.
pages.report: A report for the plant director: the <bottleneck>bottleneck</bottleneck>, its cost, the evidence.
pages.planner: Which orders to release today, in which order, to keep the <bottleneck>bottleneck</bottleneck> busy.
pages.buffer: The orders waiting in front of your <bottleneck>bottleneck</bottleneck> (the <buffer>buffer</buffer>), marked green, yellow or red.
pages.plan: Which machine will be your <bottleneck>bottleneck</bottleneck> in the coming weeks.
pages.flow: Your plant from input to output, with the <bottleneck>bottleneck</bottleneck> highlighted.
pages.shift: One clear signal per shift: is the <bottleneck>bottleneck</bottleneck> running, waiting or down.
pages.station: The screen at a machine: tap start, done and stop.
pages.value: The gain in <throughput>throughput</throughput> we predicted against the gain you measured, for finance to sign off.

bottleneck.name: Bottleneck
bottleneck.text: The one machine or step that limits how much the whole plant can ship. Also called the constraint.

throughput.name: Throughput
throughput.text: Money a product really brings in: sales price minus truly variable cost (mostly material).

capacity.name: Effective capacity
capacity.text: Hours a machine can really produce, after breaks, stops and setups are taken off.

oee.name: OEE
oee.text: How much of the planned time a machine made good parts at full speed, in %. Lost to stops, slow running and scrap.

setup.name: Setup
setup.text: Time to switch a machine from one product or colour to the next. Nothing is made meanwhile.

starved.name: Starved
starved.text: The machine is ready but has no work: the step before it did not deliver.

blocked.name: Blocked
blocked.text: The machine has finished work but cannot pass it on: the step after it is full.

buffer.name: Buffer
buffer.text: Work waiting in front of the bottleneck, so it never runs out of work.

confidence.name: Confidence
confidence.text: How sure we are of a number: high, medium or low, based on how much data backs it.

figure.title: How this is calculated
figure.periodAll: All data in the latest import
figure.calculatedBy: Calculated by the engine from your imported data. Nothing here is typed in by hand.

formulas.data_quality_score: Start at 100. Take off twice the share of rejected rows (at most 30 points), then 15, 7 or 2 points for each high, medium or low gap. Never below 0.
formulas.record_count: The number of rows that were read and accepted.
formulas.event_period_weeks: Weeks between the first and the last machine event in your data.
formulas.oee_availability: Share of the planned production time the machine was not stopped unplanned.
formulas.oee_performance: How fast the machine ran compared with its ideal speed, while running.
formulas.oee_quality: Share of the units that were good (not scrapped at this machine).
formulas.effective_capacity_h: Planned production hours, minus the share lost to unplanned stops.
formulas.task_time_median: The middle value of the measured work minutes per unit over all finished operations.
formulas.task_time_p90: The time 90% of the finished operations stayed under, in work minutes per unit.
formulas.throughput_per_unit: Sales price minus truly variable cost (mostly material).
formulas.throughput_per_constraint_min: Throughput per unit divided by the minutes the bottleneck needs per unit.
formulas.constraint_hours: A euro amount shown as hours of bottleneck time: amount ÷ throughput per bottleneck hour.

figure.isGiven: Taken from your data as it is: not a calculation.
